questions.question: What is the core principle of a 'Mobile-First' responsive design approach?
options: Websites are built only for mobile devices and cannot be opened on desktops
Base CSS styles are written for mobile screens first, and min-width queries progressively add styles for larger screens
Mobile-first relies entirely on native app store downloads
questions.explanation: Mobile-first starts with simple baseline styles for small screens, using min-width queries to progressively add complexity as screens grow.

questions.question: Which type of media query is universally used in mobile-first responsive architecture?
questions.explanation: min-width queries are the hallmark of mobile-first architecture, progressively enhancing layouts as viewports widen.

questions.question: Why is desktop-first (using max-width) often harder to maintain than mobile-first?
options: Desktop-first requires constantly overriding and cancelling out complex desktop properties for smaller screens
questions.hint: Cancelling out styles creates bloated overrides.
questions.explanation: Desktop-first requires writing complex desktop styles first and then writing repetitive overrides to dismantle them on mobile devices.

questions.question: What is a standard breakpoint value for tablet devices in most modern design systems?
questions.explanation: 768px (equivalent to iPad portrait width) is the standard medium (md) breakpoint for tablets.

questions.question: In a mobile-first stylesheet, where should default styling (e.g. single-column card layout) be placed?
options: Outside of any media queries at the top level of the stylesheet
At the very bottom of the stylesheet
questions.hint: Default styles apply to mobile without media queries.
questions.explanation: In mobile-first design, base styles for mobile screens are defined without media queries; media queries only add enhancement for larger screens.
